title: Pastry, puff, custard or cream filled, iced or not iced

content.title: About
content.content: Pastries made from puff pastry with custard or cream filling are a popular dessert that can be glazed or left plain. The flaky dough gives a light, crisp texture, while the filling adds richness and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puff pastry originated in France in the 17th century and quickly became the basis for many baked goods.
Cream fillings are often based on pastry cream, custard, or whipped cheese.
Glazes can be chocolate, sugar, fruit, or simply a dusting of powdered sugar.
Traditionally these pastries are served with tea or coffee in European cafés.
Mini versions, sometimes called “croissant bites,” are popular in several countries.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The puff pastry provides carbohydrates that supply quick energy.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Dough made with eggs and milk contains B1, B2, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Cream fillings made with milk and butter deliver calcium beneficial for bones.

items.title: High sugar and fat
items.content: Glaze and buttery fillings make the pastries calorie‑dense; they should be enjoyed in moderation.

items.title: Allergy to dairy and eggs
items.content: Ingredients may trigger reactions in people with milk or egg intolerance.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Using margarine in the dough can introduce trans fats, which are undesirable for heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pastries can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, served with tea or coffee, or used as a base for layered cakes. They are easy to cut into bite‑size portions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate – up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature before serving so the dough stays tender.
